subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: Level of organisation and cell structure
Movement of substances into and out of cells

questions.q: Which structure is found in a typical plant cell but not in a typical animal cell?
questions.explain: Plant cells are surrounded by a cellulose cell wall for support, whereas animal cells have only a cell membrane.

questions.q: What is the main function of the mitochondria?
options: Controlling the activities of the cell
questions.explain: Mitochondria are the site of aerobic respiration, releasing energy from glucose.

questions.q: Which sequence correctly shows increasing levels of organisation in an organism?
options: Cell → tissue → organ → organ system → organism
Tissue → cell → organ → organism → organ system
Organ → tissue → cell → organism → organ system
Cell → organ → tissue → organism → organ system
questions.explain: Cells group into tissues, tissues into organs, organs into organ systems, which together form the whole organism.

questions.q: A cell measures 0.05 mm across. Under a microscope its image measures 50 mm across. What is the magnification?
questions.explain: Magnification = image size ÷ actual size = 50 ÷ 0.05 = ×1000.

questions.q: Which reagent is used to test for reducing sugars such as glucose?
questions.explain: Benedict's solution turns from blue to brick-red when heated with a reducing sugar.

questions.q: What colour change shows that starch is present when iodine solution is added?
questions.explain: Iodine solution turns from orange-brown to blue-black in the presence of starch.

questions.q: Proteins are large molecules built from which smaller units?
questions.explain: Proteins are made from long chains of amino acids joined together.

questions.q: A student heats a food sample with Benedict's solution and it stays blue. What does this show?
questions.explain: Benedict's solution remains blue when no reducing sugar is present in the sample.

questions.q: Diffusion is best described as the net movement of particles from a region of:
options: one cell to an identical cell
questions.explain: Diffusion is the net movement of particles down a concentration gradient, from high to low concentration.

questions.q: Osmosis is the movement of water molecules across a partially permeable membrane from:
options: a dilute solution to a more concentrated solution
a concentrated solution to a more dilute solution
questions.explain: In osmosis water moves from a region of higher water potential (dilute) to lower water potential (concentrated) through a partially permeable membrane.

questions.q: Which statement about active transport is correct?
options: It moves substances against a concentration gradient using energy from respiration
It moves substances down a concentration gradient without energy
It does not require a cell membrane
questions.explain: Active transport uses energy released by respiration to move substances against their concentration gradient.

questions.q: A piece of plant tissue is placed in a concentrated sugar solution. What is most likely to happen to its cells?
options: Water leaves the cells and they become flaccid
Water enters the cells and they burst
The cells gain mass and become turgid
No net movement of water occurs
questions.explain: The solution has a lower water potential than the cells, so water leaves by osmosis and the cells become flaccid.

questions.q: What are the products of photosynthesis?
questions.explain: Photosynthesis uses carbon dioxide and water to produce glucose and oxygen.

questions.q: Which enzyme breaks down starch into maltose?
questions.explain: Amylase is a carbohydrase that digests starch into maltose.

questions.q: What is the role of bile in digestion?
options: It emulsifies fats to increase their surface area
It digests proteins into amino acids
It breaks down starch into sugars
It absorbs digested food into the blood
questions.explain: Bile emulsifies large fat droplets into smaller ones, increasing the surface area for lipase to act on.

questions.q: A plant is grown in soil lacking magnesium ions. Which problem is most likely?
options: It cannot make chlorophyll and its leaves turn yellow
It cannot make proteins and growth is stunted
It cannot absorb water through the roots
questions.explain: Magnesium ions are needed to make chlorophyll, so a deficiency causes yellowing of the leaves.

questions.q: Which type of blood vessel carries blood away from the heart?
questions.explain: Arteries carry blood away from the heart, usually at high pressure.

questions.q: Which substance in red blood cells binds to and carries oxygen?
questions.explain: Haemoglobin in red blood cells combines with oxygen to form oxyhaemoglobin.

questions.q: In a plant, which tissue transports water and mineral ions from the roots to the leaves?
questions.explain: Xylem vessels carry water and dissolved mineral ions upwards from the roots, while phloem transports dissolved sugars.

questions.q: Which change would increase the rate of transpiration from a leaf?
questions.explain: Increased wind speed removes water vapour from around the leaf, maintaining a steep concentration gradient and increasing transpiration.
